articles.title: SEBI Wants to Double the Stocks You Can Short — And India's $5 Trillion Market Is About to Get a Lot More Interesting for NRIs
articles.excerpt: India's market regulator is planning to nearly double stocks eligible for lending and borrowing from 176 to over 300, while cutting collateral from 130% to near-global levels — a move aimed at pulling retail investors away from the world's largest and riskiest derivatives market.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, India's oldest stock exchange
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors trading Indian equities through PIS accounts and GIFT City brokerages will benefit from deeper cash market liquidity and lower margin requirements, making hedging positions cheaper and more flexible
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Scraps Import Duties on Smartphone Parts and Lithium-Ion Cells — A $500 Billion Bet on Becoming the World's Electronics Factory
articles.excerpt: New Delhi removes 5% and 7.5% levies on wireless charging modules, automotive displays, and battery cells in a move that benefits Apple and Xiaomi while targeting a 28-fold production growth encore by 2030.
articles.image_caption: A printed circuit board — India's sweeping import duty cuts on electronics components aim to build a domestic manufacturing powerhouse
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors with exposure to Apple, Foxconn, Tata Electronics, and Indian EV battery plays stand to benefit as duty-free lithium-ion cell imports accelerate domestic manufacturing scale and attract fresh FDI into India's electronics corridor
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Hits Record 4.93 Million Barrels Per Day in Crude Imports — And Russia Now Supplies More Than Half
articles.excerpt: As the Strait of Hormuz flares up again, India's crude supply story is one of diversification and resilience. But LPG and LNG — the fuels that heat 335 million Indian kitchens — remain dangerously exposed.
articles.image_caption: India's crude oil imports hit a record 4.93 million barrels per day, with Russia now supplying more than half
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors worried about their Indian portfolio exposure to oil shocks should note that crude supply is well-diversified, but rising LPG and LNG costs could squeeze consumer spending and FMCG earnings — a second-order hit to Indian equities
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's UPI Goes Global — Indonesia Integration, ECB Linkage, and a 20-Country Roadmap That Could Reshape How NRIs Move Money
articles.excerpt: From Southeast Asia to Europe, India's payment rail is building cross-border corridors that could slash remittance costs and challenge Visa-Mastercard dominance — and the diaspora stands to benefit most.
articles.image_caption: India's Unified Payments Interface logo — the payment rail now operates in eight countries and is targeting twenty by FY29 (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: UPI's international expansion directly impacts NRIs through cheaper remittances, seamless travel payments, and new cross-border money corridors — potentially cutting transfer costs from 3-5% to under 1% on major diaspora corridors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Inc. Revenue Growth Hits a Two-Year High at 11.5% — But It's Pricing, Not Demand, Doing the Heavy Lifting
articles.excerpt: A Crisil analysis of 400 companies shows the strongest quarterly topline growth since mid-2024, led by autos at 22-24%. The catch: margins are under pressure, and the price-over-volume dynamic could reverse quickly.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai, India's oldest stock exchange
articles.nri_angle: NRI equity investors need to look beneath the headline revenue growth — the shift from volume to pricing-driven expansion means sector selection matters more than ever, with autos and IT leading genuine demand while commodity and pharma stocks face reversal risk.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: SBI Funds Management Prices $1.2 Billion IPO at ₹545–574 — ADIA and GIC Already In, Retail Gets Half the Pie
articles.excerpt: India's largest asset manager opens its blockbuster public offering on July 14, kicking off a $20 billion H2 IPO pipeline that includes the NSE and Reliance Jio.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai, home to India's capital markets
articles.nri_angle: NRIs with NRE/NRO demat accounts can apply for the IPO through ASBA, with 50% reserved for retail investors — a rare chance to get into India's largest fund house at listing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Forex Reserves Jump $7.26 Billion in a Week — Gold Reserves Cross $105 Billion as RBI Rebuilds Its War Chest
articles.excerpt: The sharpest weekly gain in over a month lifts reserves to $674.19 billion, still $54 billion below their pre-conflict peak, as Modi's austerity appeals and RBI intervention reshape the FX landscape for NRI remittances.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai
articles.nri_angle: Reserve levels directly affect RBI's ability to defend the rupee, which determines how many rupees NRIs get per dollar on remittances — the current rate still favours senders, but the window may narrow.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's SIP Machine Hits ₹317.81 Billion — Just ₹3 Billion Short of the All-Time Record as Mid-Cap Inflows Surge 39%
articles.excerpt: Equity mutual fund inflows rebound 26.5% in June, extending the longest positive streak on record to five years, while gold ETFs stage a dramatic comeback after May's tariff shock.
articles.image_caption: The National Stock Exchange of India in Mumbai, the backbone of the country's equity markets
articles.nri_angle: NRIs with NRE/NRO accounts can set up SIPs from abroad to ride the structural floor under Indian equities — and gold ETFs are now cheaper than physical gold after the 15% import tariff hike.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Dr. Reddy's Posts Worst Week in Three Years as Semaglutide Supply Crisis Hands Rivals the GLP-1 Prize
articles.excerpt: An impurity in the active ingredient has halted production of Obeda until at least late October, eroding the first-mover advantage that was central to Dr. Reddy's growth thesis — and opening the door for Zydus and Sun Pharma.
articles.image_caption: A semaglutide injection pen — the drug at the center of Dr. Reddy's supply crisis
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors with Indian pharma exposure face a strategic question: is the Dr. Reddy's dip a buying opportunity or a signal that GLP-1 execution risk is underpriced across the sector?
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Goldman Sachs Upgrades Rupee Forecast to 94 — What NRIs Should Know Before the Remittance Window Closes
articles.excerpt: The Wall Street bank sees the dollar-rupee pair plateauing as RBI measures, record bond inflows, and an unwind of rate-hike bets reshape the currency outlook. For NRIs, the 95+ remittance rate may not last.
articles.image_caption: Indian rupee currency notes — NRIs face a narrowing window for favorable remittance rates
articles.nri_angle: NRIs sending money home face a narrowing window: the rupee's current 95+ rate may tighten toward 94 if Goldman's forecast plays out. NRE deposit rates at 7%+ tax-free amplify the urgency.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Earnings Season Opens With a Bang — J.P. Morgan Sees Nifty at 27,000 as TCS Delivers and Markets Shake Off Iran Fears
articles.excerpt: After surviving a 1,677-point Sensex crash mid-week, Indian markets closed just 0.3% lower as TCS beat estimates and foreign investors bought the dip. Here's what NRI investors should watch as Q1 results pour in.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai — India's markets showed resilience this week despite geopolitical shocks
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors face a rare setup: Indian markets absorbed a brutal crash in 48 hours, earnings season has started strong, and J.P. Morgan sees 11.5% upside. The playbook favors banking and IT sector bets.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Shapoorji Pallonji Launches $650 Million Dollar Bond With BlackRock Backing — What NRI Investors Should Know About India's Hottest Debt Deal
articles.excerpt: The Tata Sons-linked conglomerate's debut dollar bond at 14.5% yield has drawn Deutsche Bank as arranger and BlackRock as a likely investor, signalling growing global appetite for Indian high-yield corporate credit.
articles.image_caption: iMahesh via wikimedia (BY-SA)
articles.nri_angle: The deal signals maturing Indian corporate debt markets with yields far above NRE deposits — NRI investors can access this via global credit funds like BlackRock's Asia-focused vehicle, diversifying beyond traditional FD and equity exposure.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Rate-Hike Fears Collapse as Traders Dump Bets in Record $2.65 Billion Swap Day — What It Means for NRI Portfolios
articles.excerpt: The five-year OIS rate has plunged from 6.9% to 6.1% since April as markets abandon expectations of aggressive RBI tightening, signalling a turning point for Indian bonds, bank stocks and NRE deposit rates.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai
articles.nri_angle: The rate-hike scare's end means NRE/NRO deposit rates may have peaked, Indian bonds are rallying, and the rupee remittance window is narrowing — NRIs should reassess fixed-income allocations and remittance timing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Survived a Record $48 Billion Foreign Exodus — And Came Out Stronger. Here's What NRI Investors Need to Know
articles.excerpt: Domestic investors adding $3.5 billion a month cushioned the blow as foreign money fled. Now FPIs are returning, tax barriers are falling and Bloomberg bond index inclusion looms — a turning point for India allocations.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building on Dalal Street in Mumbai
articles.nri_angle: India's structural market resilience — proven by $3.5B/month domestic SIP flows absorbing record FPI outflows — combined with new tax breaks and bond index inclusion, makes the case for NRIs to reassess India equity and fixed-income allocations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Silver Import Crackdown Sends Premiums to Six-Month High — What NRI Bullion Buyers Need to Know
articles.excerpt: Imports have nearly halted after New Delhi hiked duties from 6% to 15% and restricted silver bars, grain, and powder. Domestic premiums have surged to $6.50 an ounce above global prices, and the squeeze is just getting started.
articles.image_caption: Silver bullion bars — India's import restrictions have created acute domestic shortages
articles.nri_angle: NRIs who buy silver bullion in India during visits, invest in Indian silver ETFs, or send money home for family jewellery purchases face a fundamentally different market. Premiums have flipped from discounts to double-digit surcharges, silver ETF outflows have released stored metal that is now drying up, and the import duty hike means any silver entering India costs 15% more at the border. For NRI investors holding Indian silver ETF units, the NAV may benefit from rising local premiums — but liquidity risk is growing as the physical market tightens.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The India-US Trade Deal Is '99% Done' — So Why Can't They Close It?
articles.excerpt: Commerce Minister Goyal says India won't sign until it secures a tariff edge over Pakistan and ASEAN rivals. Section 301 hearings in Washington could push Indian tariffs from 18% to 32%. For NRI exporters and IT workers, the stakes keep rising.
articles.image_caption: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal has said India will not implement the trade deal until it secures a competitive edge
articles.nri_angle: The India-US trade deal directly affects NRI professionals, business owners, and investors. Indian IT companies that employ tens of thousands of H-1B workers depend on favourable trade terms. NRI-owned export businesses face 18% tariffs that could jump to 28-32% under Section 301. And the deal's outcome will shape FDI flows, market sentiment, and the rupee — all of which touch NRI portfolios.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Inc. Hedged a Record $120 Billion in June as the Rupee Swings Between War and Central Bank Muscle
articles.excerpt: Corporate FX hedging hit an all-time high as the rupee whipsawed between 94.96 and 95.60 this week. Goldman Sachs sees the dollar-rupee at 94 in three months. Here's what the hedging boom means for NRI remittances.
articles.image_caption: Indian rupee currency notes — the rupee traded between 94.96 and 95.60 this week amid geopolitical volatility
articles.nri_angle: The rupee's trajectory directly affects every NRI sending money to India. With corporate hedging at record levels and Goldman Sachs forecasting USD/INR at 94 in three months (implying a stronger rupee), NRIs face a classic timing dilemma on remittances. The RBI's dollar-inflow measures could strengthen the rupee medium-term, meaning locking in today's 95+ rate for large transfers may be advantageous. NRE deposit rates, which are linked to rupee liquidity conditions, could also shift as RBI manages the inflow surge.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: TCS Beats Revenue Estimates as AI Business Crosses $2.6 Billion — What NRI Investors Should Know
articles.excerpt: India's largest IT exporter posted 14% revenue growth, restarted hiring after three years, and expanded partnerships with Anthropic and Mistral. The dividend cheque lands July 31.
articles.image_caption: TCS Gitanjali Park campus in Kolkata, one of the company's major technology hubs
articles.nri_angle: TCS is one of the largest H-1B employers and a cornerstone holding for NRI investors. The $2.6B AI revenue run rate, dividend declaration, and hiring restart all directly impact diaspora portfolios and career prospects.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Foreign Investors Pour $1 Billion Into Indian Real Estate in Q2 — A 454% Surge That NRIs Should Watch
articles.excerpt: Institutional investment in Indian property hit $2.68 billion in the April-June quarter, with Chennai and Bengaluru overtaking Mumbai as the top targets. Here's what the data means for diaspora buyers.
articles.image_caption: Mumbai's commercial skyline — foreign investors poured  billion into Indian real estate in Q2 2026 (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRIs are significant property investors in India under FEMA rules. The surge in foreign institutional capital validates India's real estate thesis, while rupee weakness near 95.4/$ offers diaspora buyers an effective discount on INR-denominated assets.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Gold Hits ₹1.44 Lakh, SGBs Are at a Premium, and New Issuances Are Dead — Here's How NRIs Should Buy Gold Now
articles.excerpt: With 24-carat gold up ₹11,000 in 2026 and Sovereign Gold Bonds no longer being issued, NRI investors need to rethink how they access India's favourite asset class.
articles.image_caption: Gold bars — the metal has climbed to ₹1.44 lakh per 10 grams in 2026 as NRIs weigh their options (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Gold remains culturally and financially significant for NRIs. With SGBs effectively closed to new buyers and secondary-market premiums eroding value, diaspora investors need updated strategies for gold allocation across India and the US.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Foreign Investors Pour $1.5 Billion Into Indian Banks in Biggest Buying Spree Since 2025
articles.excerpt: Policy support, cheaper valuations, and easing rate-hike fears are drawing FPIs back to Indian financials after 18 months of record outflows — but oil prices threaten the recovery.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai, India's financial capital
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors with Indian bank ETFs, HDFC ADRs, and NRE deposits benefit directly from the FPI flow reversal and elimination of capital gains and withholding taxes on foreign investments.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Razorpay to the NSE: Inside India's $51 Billion IPO Pipeline That Could Rewrite Market History
articles.excerpt: With 251 companies in the queue and mega listings from the National Stock Exchange, Razorpay, and Reliance Jio on the horizon, India's second-half IPO wave promises to be its most consequential yet.
articles.image_caption: The National Stock Exchange of India building in Mumbai's Bandra Kurla Complex
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors can participate in Indian IPOs through demat accounts linked to NRE/NRO accounts. Razorpay's reverse flip from US to India represents a structural trend bringing diaspora-connected companies to Indian exchanges.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sensex Crashes 1,677 Points as Trump Declares Iran Deal 'Over' — Oil Surges, Rupee Hits One-Month Low
articles.excerpt: Indian markets suffered their worst single-day fall in three months after the US-Iran ceasefire collapsed, sending Brent crude past $79, the rupee to 95.55, and the India VIX up 26 percent — a triple blow for NRI investors watching from abroad.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai, home to the Sensex index
articles.nri_angle: India imports 85% of its crude oil — the Iran-driven spike threatens higher inflation, a weaker rupee, and delayed rate cuts, directly impacting NRI remittances, mutual fund returns, and property investment plans.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Largest Mutual Fund House Is Going Public — and Abu Dhabi and Singapore's Sovereign Funds Are Already In
articles.excerpt: SBI Funds Management's $1.2 billion IPO kicks off a wave of blockbuster listings that could raise $50 billion in the second half of 2026.
articles.image_caption: State Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors can participate in the SBI Funds IPO through Indian demat accounts; the listing is a proxy for India's mutual fund revolution driven by millions of SIP investors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Private Banks Just Posted Their Strongest Quarter in Over a Year — and Wall Street Is Raising Its Bets
articles.excerpt: HDFC Bank, Axis Bank, and YES Bank report double-digit loan growth in Q1 FY27, lifting the Sensex past 78,200 and extending the market's longest winning streak of 2026
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai, home to the Sensex benchmark
articles.nri_angle: Indian bank stocks are among the most popular NRI equity positions, and Q1 FY27 updates showing accelerating loan growth and record foreign bond inflows signal a strengthening investment case for diaspora capital.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Biggest Healthcare IPO Is Coming — Manipal Health Just Got SEBI's Green Light for a $1.2 Billion Listing
articles.excerpt: The Temasek-backed hospital chain, which runs 48 hospitals and more than 12,000 beds across 14 states, is targeting a late July debut that will test investor appetite for India's booming private healthcare sector.
articles.image_caption: A modern hospital facility in India — Manipal Health operates 48 hospitals with over 12,000 beds across 14 states (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRIs who use Indian hospitals for medical tourism can now invest in the sector's growth — Manipal's IPO offers exposure to a healthcare boom driven by rising insurance penetration and complex care demand.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
